claim.quote: We present new νμ→νe, νμ→νμ, ν̄μ→ν̄e, and ν̄μ→ν̄μ oscillation measurements by the NOvA experiment, with a 50% increase in neutrino-mode beam exposure over the previously reported results.

date.note: Published as Phys. Rev. D 106, 032004 (2022); posted to arXiv 2021-08-18.
date.quote: An Improved Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters by the NOvA Experiment

key_value_text.quote: with $Δm^{2}_{32} = (2.41\pm0.07)\times 10^{-3}$ eV$^2$ and $\sin^2θ_{23} = 0.57^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$ ... excluded by $>3σ$ for the inverted mass ordering, and values around $δ_\text{CP} = 3π/2$ in the normal ordering which are disfavored at 2$σ$ confidence
key_value_text.value: Best fit: Δm²₃₂ = (2.41±0.07)×10⁻³ eV², sin²θ₂₃ = 0.57 +0.03/−0.04 (upper octant), normal mass ordering preferred; δ_CP near π/2 excluded at >3σ for inverted ordering, values near 3π/2 disfavored at 2σ for normal ordering

name: An Improved Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters by the NOvA Experiment

significance.locator: arXiv:2108.08219, abstract (no single significance/sigma reported for a parameter measurement)
significance.note: A multi-parameter oscillation measurement, not a single-significance discovery/observation; specific exclusions (e.g. delta_CP near pi/2 for inverted ordering) are quoted at different confidence levels in key_value_text.

summary.plain: NOvA's most precise look yet at how neutrinos change type on their 810-kilometre trip, favouring one particular ordering of neutrino masses and one range for how matter-antimatter symmetry might be broken for neutrinos, without settling either question.
summary.technical: Joint νμ/ν̄μ disappearance and νe/ν̄e appearance fit with 50% more neutrino-mode exposure than the previous NOvA release: Δm²₃₂=(2.41±0.07)×10⁻³ eV², sin²θ₂₃=0.57 (upper octant), normal ordering favored; δ_CP near π/2 excluded at >3σ assuming inverted ordering.

title: An Improved Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters by the NOvA Experiment
why_it_matters: Determining the neutrino mass ordering and the CP-violating phase delta_CP are two of the biggest open questions in neutrino physics; NOvA's beam and atmospheric-scale baseline give it direct sensitivity to both, in combination with results from other experiments such as T2K.
